chapter: Hampton, New York and Lee's own band
title: Norman Granz, tennis and the origin of Jazz at the Philharmonic
summary: Lee gave Granz names of musicians to call; Granz took the idea to clubs and Lee believes this led to Jazz at the Philharmonic.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Norman used to hang out there?

Norman and I used to hang out together, and Norman and I used to play tennis together. But it's a funny thing how a guy will have an idea. You know, you have a million dollars in your pocket and you just don't realize it. I used to call all the musicians to get these things, you know, but I've always been a sports freak. I like to go to football games, baseball games, basketball games --and at that time I didn't play golf. I loved to play tennis.

And I started giving Norman names of the guys to call and Norman took it a step further. He went to the different clubs, and he used to have sessions at the 331 Club on a Monday night, he'd have one at the Trouville on Sunday afternoon and then he'd have a session someplace else, you know? And I'm certain this is how he came up with Jazz at the Philharmonic.
Well, at that time he was a film editor at MGM or something, wasn't he?
Well, I never did know him as a film editor.
Oh? You read that, did you?
Yeah. I didn't know him then, so I don't know.

Well, all I knew, I used to take him around with us all the time and all I knew was he had gone to UCLA for a year or two, and he used to play pretty good tennis. And the big tennis court over on La Cienega just off of Wilshire, and this is where I really met him, you know, because this was where tennis players, you know, they're really gamblers, and that's where they used to have big gambling matches, and I took him over to meet this young black guy who was an excellent tennis player - but he had never had a chance to play any of the heavy-weights. His name was Jimmy MacDaniels.
And that's how Norman and I became friends, because he liked jazz, and he was always around -- but he started to give all the names of the musicians, and that is a fact.
